Music is the only language that requires no translation and yet remains perpetually untranslatable. A cello draws its bow across the dusk and something in the chest cavity responds, some resonance older than vocabulary, older than the naming of things.

Consider the silence between notes. It is not emptiness but architecture... the scaffolding upon which melody constructs its brief and trembling cathedral. Without those pauses, sound becomes mere noise, a river without banks, flooding everything, nourishing nothing.

The pianist's hands are cartographers mapping territories that exist only in the moment of their traversal. Each performance is a country visited once and never again, its borders dissolving the instant the final chord surrenders to the air.

We say music moves us. But perhaps it is more accurate to say it reveals the movement already occurring within, the tidal pull of emotions we had forgotten to name. The vibration of a string mirrors some sympathetic frequency in the marrow... and we call this beauty, for lack of a more precise word.
